posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Pool That Belongs to the House
posts.alt: A Santaluz Spanish-colonial estate backyard at golden hour: a long rectangular pool with ivory Bedrosians travertine coping and deck, a raised stainless steel Diamond Spas spa spilling into the pool, a white plaster arched loggia beneath a clay barrel-tile roof on the two-story home, teak chaises with linen cushions, mature olive trees, lavender and agave in gravel beds, and neighboring tile-roof estate homes close by on both sides and across the rolling hills
posts.hook: A pool should look like it was always part of the house — not something added to the yard later.
posts.caption:
Stand in the loggia and look out. The pool runs on the same line as the arches, the travertine picks up the warmth of the plaster, and the spa sits exactly where the evening light lands. Nothing competes with the architecture. It simply carries it outside.

That's the real work on a property like this. Not the size of the water, but the alignment — where the pool starts relative to the doors, how the coping meets the deck, which trees stay and which views get framed. When those decisions are made first, the finishes almost choose themselves.

The result is quiet. The kind of quiet that only reads as expensive once you notice how little is out of place.

The selections:
• Bedrosians ivory travertine coping & deck
• Diamond Spas stainless steel spa with spillover
• mature olive trees, lavender & agave in gravel beds
• teak chaises in natural linen

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · Coronado Cottage
posts.alt: The front of a Coronado cedar-shingle Craftsman cottage in late-afternoon light: weathered natural shingle siding, white trim, a deep front porch with tapered columns and a dark green door, a wide Belgard Mega-Arbel paver driveway in warm sand and grey tones leading to a carriage-style garage door, a matching paver front walk, clipped boxwood edging, an olive tree, agave and silver groundcover, a low white picket fence with climbing roses, FX Luminaire path lights, tall palms, and neighboring cottages close by on both sides of the tree-lined street
posts.hook: On an island of small lots, the driveway is half the front yard. It might as well be beautiful.
posts.caption:
Coronado lots are narrow and the houses sit close to the street, which means the driveway is never just a driveway. It's the largest single surface anyone sees when they arrive — and on a lot this size, it's often half the front yard.

So we treat it like part of the garden. A large-format paver in warm sand and grey, laid in a random pattern so it reads more like old stone than new concrete. The same paver turns and becomes the front walk, so the eye travels one continuous path to the porch. Boxwood keeps the edges crisp, the olive tree gives the front some height, and low path lights carry the whole thing into the evening without lighting up the street.

A cottage that looks like it's been loved for a long time. Which is exactly the point.

The selections:
• Belgard Mega-Arbel paver driveway & front walk
• clipped boxwood edging with olive, agave & silver groundcover
• FX Luminaire path lighting

posts.style: Craft & Process · The Stone Is the Last Inch
posts.alt: A canyon-edge Kensington backyard at blue hour beside a warm-grey stucco Spanish Revival home: a tall outdoor fireplace clad in Eldorado Stone stacked limestone veneer with a fire burning, a curved stone-capped seat wall wrapping a Techo-Bloc Aberdeen slab paver terrace, two deep lounge chairs, bougainvillea on the wall, an olive tree and agave lit by warm FX Luminaire uplights, a wrought-iron lantern beside an arched door, and neighboring tile-roof homes with lit windows close by and across the canyon
posts.hook: The stone you see on a fireplace is about an inch and a half deep. Everything that matters is behind it.
posts.caption:
Stone veneer is the part everyone points at. It's also the thinnest layer of the whole build.

Behind it sits the real fireplace: a footing sized for the weight, a block core, a properly lined firebox and flue, and a moisture barrier and scratch coat so the veneer bonds to the structure instead of just sticking to it. On a canyon edge like this one, the footing and the drainage behind the seat wall get as much attention as anything you'll ever see — the slope doesn't care how good the stone looks.

Only after all of that does the veneer go on, piece by piece, joints dressed by hand so it reads as stacked limestone rather than a product from a pallet. Then the lighting: two warm uplights, one on the stone, one in the olive, and nothing else.

You'll never see the first ninety percent. It's the reason the last inch still looks like this in fifteen years.

The selections:
• Eldorado Stone stacked limestone veneer fireplace
• stone-capped curved seat wall
• Techo-Bloc Aberdeen slab paver terrace
• FX Luminaire uplighting
• olive, agave & bougainvillea

posts.hook: Happy Thanksgiving, San Diego. Wherever your table is today, we hope it's a long one.
posts.caption:
Today isn't for selling anything. It's for the people around the table.

We're grateful for the families who invite us into their homes, for the neighborhoods we get to work in, and for a city where late November still lets you eat outside with the doors open. Thank you, sincerely, from Gio, Mike and the whole crew.

If you're lucky enough to set the table outdoors this year, this is the kind of setting we love to design for: one long table that seats everyone, a pergola overhead so the lights have somewhere to hang, a fire close enough to take the edge off once the sun drops, and the grill a few steps away so whoever's cooking never misses the conversation.

The selections:
• Trex pergola with cafe lighting
• Belgard Urbana paver patio
• Warming Trends linear fire table
• Blaze built-in grill in a stone-clad outdoor kitchen

Enjoy the day. And whenever you're ready to think about your own long table, DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Trust & Difference · Drone Aerial · One Honest Number
posts.alt: Top-down drone aerial of an Olivenhain backyard: a sculpted SYNLawn Golf putting green with three cups and flags, fringed by a light-grey Techo-Bloc Industria slab paver terrace with a round fire pit and four chairs, decomposed granite paths, rows of citrus trees and a small olive grove, ornamental grasses and agave, the black standing-seam metal roof of a white board-and-batten modern farmhouse along the bottom edge, and neighboring houses, pools and backyards on every side
posts.hook: There's no sale on this page today. There never will be.
posts.caption:
Today the internet is full of countdowns and percentages. We don't run them, and we'd rather say why than stay quiet.

Every project we take on is priced from a walk-through and a line-item scope — the real materials, the real crew time, the real subcontractors. It's one honest number. If it could be 30% lower this week, it wasn't honest the week before. And a discount on a backyard usually shows up later somewhere you'd rather it didn't: in the base, the drainage, the finish.

So instead of a sale, here's what stays the same every day of the year: a design you sign off on before anything is built, a direct line to Gio and Mike, and a return visit ten months after we finish to make sure it's still right.

This view is the whole plan from above — a putting green sculpted into the lawn, a paver terrace with a fire pit at its edge, and citrus and olive rows that make a family yard feel like it's been there for decades.

The selections:
• SYNLawn Golf putting green
• Techo-Bloc Industria slab paver terrace
• round gas fire pit
• citrus rows, olive grove & decomposed granite paths
